# Staff leave

Seven people work at Larkfield, including two part-time assistants. Because kiln firings must be supervised, holidays need to be planned so the studio is never left without a trained potter.

## Booking holidays

Full-time staff get twenty-five days of paid holiday plus bank holidays; part-time staff receive a proportional share. Requests are made through the shared calendar at least three weeks in advance and approved by Sam. Nobody can book more than ten consecutive working days between June and August, the busiest period for wedding orders. If two potters ask for the same week, whoever booked first keeps it.

## Sickness

Anyone who is unwell should phone Sam before eight in the morning so that firings can be rescheduled. Sick days are recorded separately and never deducted from holiday allowance. A doctor's note is needed after seven calendar days. Someone who falls ill during a holiday can reclaim those days by providing a note.

## Parental leave

Staff who become parents are entitled to the statutory leave, and the studio adds two weeks of fully paid leave on top. We ask for as much notice as possible so a temporary assistant can be trained in packing and glazing before the absence begins.
